item.title: Biman flight makes emergency landing in Rome
item.description:
A Biman Bangladesh Airlines flight from Toronto to Dhaka made an emergency landing at Rome’s Fiumicino Airport due to a technical issue and remained grounded there for at least six hours, officials said.
A public relations official of Biman Bangladesh Airlines confirmed the development on Friday evening, saying the aircraft was grounded after undergoing technical inspections following the emergency landing.
“The aircraft underwent a technical check after landing. Following an initial inspection, the authorities declared it grounded,” the official said, requesting anonymity.
Around 250 passengers were on board the flight.
The national flag carrier is working to arrange alternative flights, accommodation and meals for the affected passengers, the official added.

item.title: Gas shortage intensifies load shedding in Chittagong
item.description:
The partial resumption of operations at the floating LNG terminal in Moheshkhali of Cox’s Bazar has brought only limited relief to Chittagong, where a prolonged gas shortage continues to disrupt electricity generation and worsen daily load shedding across the region.
The LNG terminal resumed operations after remaining shut for nearly two weeks because of a technical fault. However, the restoration has not been sufficient to meet the region's energy demand.
As a result, households and businesses in Chittagong experience frequent power outages, with many residents reporting five to six hours of load shedding every day. Rural communities are facing even longer interruptions.
According to the Bangladesh Power Development Board (BPDB), Chittagong has 28 power plants powered by gas, furnace oil, coal and hydropower. Six of those plants were out of operation on August 3 due to mechanical problems, fuel shortages or scheduled operating patterns.
Although the region's installed generation capacity exceeds 4,600 megawatts, actual production has dropped significantly because gas-fired plants are unable to operate at full capacity.
Official data show that electricity generation reached 2,819.14 MW during off-peak hours and 3,302.60 MW during peak hours on August 3. The BPDB reported electricity demand of 1,352.96 MW during off-peak hours and 1,477.2 MW during peak hours, with load shedding recorded at 65 MW and 62 MW respectively.
Consumers, however, said that the official figures do not reflect the reality on the ground, adding that power cuts have become much more frequent and prolonged.
Residents across the city say repeated outages have disrupted daily life and damaged electrical appliances due to constant voltage fluctuations. In rural parts of Chittagong, some areas are experiencing six to seven hours of power cuts each day, making living conditions increasingly difficult during the hot summer months.
The gas shortage has also forced major government-owned power plants to reduce output. Two 210 MW units at the Raozan power station, with a combined capacity of 420 MW, have remained shut because of inadequate gas supply.
The 225 MW Shikalbaha gas-fired power plant has also scaled back production. Plant officials said full-capacity operation requires about 37 million cubic feet of gas per day, but the facility has recently been receiving only 28 to 30 million cubic feet, limiting electricity generation to around 183-184 MW.
According to Karnaphuli Gas Distribution Company Limited (KGDCL), Chittagong's daily gas demand stands at approximately 350 million cubic feet, while current supply is only 200-220 million cubic feet, leaving a daily shortfall of up to 150 million cubic feet. The deficit has affected residential, commercial and transport sectors in addition to electricity generation.
KGDCL Managing Director Engineer Md Salahuddin said that it will take several more days before gas supply returns to normal.
RPGCL Manager Imtiaz Kamal Chowdhury said one terminal has resumed supplying around 180 million cubic feet of gas per day alongside another terminal supplying about 570 million cubic feet.
Following repairs carried out with the assistance of foreign specialists, gas transmission has resumed gradually. However, authorities acknowledge that restoring full electricity generation and stabilising power supply across the region will take additional time.

item.title: Shama Obaed: Govt working to curb syndicates exploiting students looking to study abroad
item.description:
State Minister for Foreign Affairs Shama Obaed Islam on Friday said the government is working to curb unscrupulous syndicates and brokers who exploit Bangladeshi students seeking to pursue higher education abroad by charging them excessive money.
“Unscrupulous syndicates or brokers take advantage of our students, who have to pay extremely high amounts of money to go abroad. The government is obviously aware of the issue and is working on it,” she said.
The state minister said while addressing the inaugural session of the two-day 14th International Education Expo 2026, organized by the Foreign Admission and Career Development Consultants Association of Bangladesh (FACD-CAB), at a city hotel.
This year the fair brought together representatives from 30 countries to provide consultancy services for around 300 world-class educational institutions around the world.
Shama Obaed said the foreign ministry has already opened a migration wing for the first time to address the migration related problems. The sole responsibility of this newly opened wing is to address all sorts of migration related problems.
She urged FACD-CAB and others concerned to help the wing by providing necessary information to contain the unscrupulous syndicates in the student migration process.
“Together, we have to work in a unison way here. We have to work together to bring these broker syndicates under the law. They are unfairly destroying the future of our children (students),” she said.
The state minister said the foreign ministry is ready to cooperate with FACD-CAB to make the migration process more transparent and accountable and to help it provide better services to Bangladeshi students.
She asked FACD-CAB to submit in writing its demands and problems so that the issues could be brought to the attention of the Prime Minister as well as the Foreign Ministry together with other concerned ministries, including the Education, Finance and Home ministries, could fulfill their demands and address the problems.
Shama Obaed stressed the importance of creating a safe and investment-friendly environment in Bangladesh so that students attained overseas education and experiences can return home and contribute to the country's development.
“We certainly want our children to go abroad and study. But at the same time, we need to create a safe, investment-friendly and secure environment in Bangladesh where they can return, invest and become entrepreneurs and thus help the government build the country,” she said.
Describing education as an important instrument of diplomacy, she said the Ministry of Foreign Affairs will continue to encourage educational and research partnerships between Bangladesh and other countries.
Bangladesh's missions abroad can help connect Bangladeshi institutions with international universities, facilitate academic cooperation and support the legitimate interests and welfare of Bangladeshi students.
Referring to the national budget for 2026-2027 fiscal year, the state minister said the government has given the highest-ever allocation to the education sector in the latest budget, reflecting its priority to education.
The International Education fair, a flagship international education event, started at Pan Pacific Sonargaon Hotel, bringing together education consultants, international university representatives, students, and stakeholders under one platform.
Visitors need prior registration to visit the education fair from 10:00am to 8:00pm.
Visitors get scope to interact directly with representatives of universities from different countries and receive guidance on scholarships, financial aid, tuition fees, visa processing and career planning.

item.title: Mir Helal: July Uprising belongs to people, not any group
item.description:
State Minister for Land and Chittagong Hill Tracts Affairs, Barrister Mir Mohammed Helal Uddin, said it is both inaccurate and misleading to portray the July-August 2024 mass uprising as the achievement of any single individual or group.
"No one can claim ownership of this mass uprising. It belongs to the 18 crore people of Bangladesh," he said.
He said the true outcome of the mass uprising was realized when the people resolved that they would no longer tolerate oppression and that the authoritarian government had to be removed.
He made the remarks while addressing a discussion titled "Fascism, July Revolution and Today's Bangladesh" as the chief guest at the July Memorial Hall of the Chittagong Press Club on Friday afternoon.
The discussion was jointly organized by the Chittagong Press Club and the Chittagong Metropolitan Union of Journalists (CMUJ).
City BNP Convener Ershad Ullah, MP, and Abu Sufian, MP, among others, addressed the event as special guests.
He said Bangladesh had been heavily burdened by the Awami League's 15 years of misrule, during which BNP leaders and activists were subjected to enforced disappearances, severe torture, and false cases.
He added that people from various professions, including journalists with dissenting views, also faced repression, ultimately leading to the July-August mass uprising as a response to years of oppression.
Mir Helal said the uprising was not intended to bring anyone to state power or government; rather, it was fought to establish Bangladesh as a truly independent and sovereign nation.
Zahidul Karim Kachi, president of the Chittagong Press Club, delivered the welcome address. The discussion was moderated by the club's General Secretary Golam Mawla Murad and Joint Secretary Meah Mohammed Arif.
CMUJ President Mohammad Shah Nawaz presided over the event.
Among others, Chittagong University Vice Chancellor Dr Mohammad Al-Forkan, Premier University Vice Chancellor Prof Dr Nasrul Quadir, Chittagong Development Authority Chairman Engineer Belayet Hossain, Chittagong City BNP Joint Convener MA Aziz, Chittagong District Bar Association President Advocate Tarique Ahmed, Press Club Vice President Mustafa Nayyem, Chittagong Metropolitan Union of Journalists General Secretary Saleh Noman, and Advocate Abdus Sattar, an injured July uprising participant and former president of the Chittagong District Bar Association, also spoke at the program.

item.title: Bobby Hajjaj: Youth to be prepared with proper skills before going to Japan
item.description:
State Minister for Primary and Mass Education, Bobby Hajjaj on Friday said Bangladeshi youths will be prepared according to international standards through language education, technical skills and technological knowledge considering the demands of the international labor market, including Japan.
He said the government's goal is not only to send manpower abroad, but also to develop skilled, language-proficient and world-class human resources.
The state minister made the remarks at a view-exchange meeting with Bangladeshi students, professionals and community representatives living in Osaka and Kobe at a local community center in Osaka, Japan.
"Bangladesh's youths are our greatest strength. The government is continuously working to develop them with international-standard language education, technical skills and technological capabilities," he said.
If skilled manpower can be created according to the demands of the labor market of developed countries like Japan, it will make an important contribution to the country's economy, employment and foreign earnings," Bobby Hajjaj added.
He said necessary policy and institutional initiatives will be taken to further strengthen language education, skill development and quality technical education.
The experiences and recommendations of expatriate Bangladeshis will be considered with importance through coordination with the relevant ministries and agencies, he continued.
Assuring that the issue of ensuring that no talented student misses the opportunity for higher education abroad only due to financial constraints will be given due importance, Bobby Hajjaj said Bangladeshi students studying abroad are important assets for the country.
Their experiences and practical suggestions will play an important role in formulating future policies on education, skill development and human resource formation, he said.
Participants at the meeting emphasized improving the quality of Japanese language education in Bangladesh, introducing a national accreditation system for language education institutions and establishing specialized training institutes for language teachers.
They also called for integrating technical and vocational education and training (TVET) with information technology education.
They also proposed policy support to utilize the skills acquired by young people returning home after training in Japan in the engineering, technology and automotive industries.
Responding to the recommendations, the state minister said the government would work with importance to improve the quality of Japanese language education, formulate a quality control system, enhance teachers' skills and expand technical education suitable for the international labor market.
He also said policy support would be ensured to utilize the knowledge acquired by returning expatriates in the country's industrial and production sectors.
Officials from the Bangladesh Embassy in Tokyo, Bangladeshi students studying at different universities in Japan, expatriate professionals, businesspeople and community leaders attended the exchange meeting.

CCGP approves procurement of since cargo of LNG from Aramco Trading Singapore
item.description:
The Cabinet Committee on Government Purchase (CCGP) on Friday approved the procurement of one cargo of liquefied natural gas (LNG) from Aramco Trading Singapore, a fully-owned subsidiary of Saudi Aramco based in Singapore, under a government-to-government (G2G) arrangement to help meet the country’s growing energy demand.
The approval came at the eighth meeting of the CCGP for the 2026-27 fiscal year, held virtually with Finance Minister Amir Khasru Mahmud Chowdhury in the chair on the weekly holiday.
The committee approved the proposal to purchase one LNG cargo from Aramco Trading Singapore for delivery on August 11-12, 2026 through the direct procurement method under the G2G framework.
The LNG will be purchased at a price of $21.55 per MMBtu, according to officials.
However, the committee again did not consider another proposal relating to a long-term LNG procurement arrangement with Gunvor USA LLC.
The Energy and Mineral Resources Division withdrew its proposal, like the Thursday meeting seeking approval for the direct purchase of LNG from Gunvor USA LLC under a G2G arrangement for the period from 2026 to 2038, before it could be placed for the committee’s consideration.
Bangladesh has been importing LNG to supplement declining domestic natural gas production and ensure a stable supply of fuel for power generation and industrial use.
The latest approval is expected to support the country’s gas supply by facilitating timely delivery of an LNG cargo during August.
The country's gas supply is gradually returning to normal after the partial restoration of the Excelerate Energy-operated floating storage and regasification unit (FSRU) at Maheshkhali, easing a nationwide shortage that disrupted power generation, industries, CNG stations and household cooking for more than two weeks.
The crisis began on July 21 when a fire damaged the FSRU’s boiler-related electrical systems, forcing the suspension of LNG regasification from one of the country’s two floating LNG terminals.
The outage cut around 450 million cubic feet of gas per day from the national grid, significantly affecting electricity production and industrial operations.
Following repair work by local and foreign engineers, the terminal has resumed partial operations, supplying about 115 million cubic feet of gas per day, with output expected to increase in phases.
Energy Minister Iqbal Hassan Mahmood on Thursday said gas supply should return to normal within two to three days as repairs continue.
Bangladesh currently faces a daily gas demand of about 3,800 to 4,000 million cubic feet against supply of roughly 2,600 million cubic feet, making imported LNG crucial to meeting domestic demand.
The latest disruption has once again highlighted the country’s growing dependence on LNG imports and the vulnerability of its gas supply system to disruptions at a single FSRU.

item.title: Long queues persist at Dhaka CNG stations amid gas supply woes
item.description:
Long queues of vehicles persisted at compressed natural gas (CNG) filling stations across the capital on Friday as gas supply remained unstable, forcing drivers to wait for hours to refuel.
The prolonged shortage, driven by inadequate pipeline pressure and irregular gas supply, has left CNG auto-rickshaws, buses and private cars lining up at filling stations around the clock, disrupting transport services and causing widespread inconvenience to commuters.
After visiting filling stations in Mohakhali, Tejgaon, Kallyanpur, Shyamoli and Gabtoli, it was found that gas shortages continue across the city. Stations resume dispensing gas when supply is restored but are forced to suspend operations once it runs out. Gas supplied overnight lasted until early morning at some stations, but many had no supply after that.
The shortage has also disrupted public transport, as buses and CNG-powered vehicles remain stranded in long queues at filling stations. Commuters, particularly on working days, are struggling to find transport for office and other essential travel. Many have been forced to walk long distances or pay higher fares for alternative transport.
"We received gas around 9:30pm and started dispensing it immediately. But since dawn, there has been no gas in the line," said Tarique, a sales employee at Akij CNG Filling Station in Tejgaon.
Filling station operators attributed the crisis to inadequate gas supply from the national grid and low pipeline pressure, saying the lack of pressure prevents them from operating compressors efficiently and safely. As a result, they are able to serve only about half the usual number of vehicles.
The shortage has also disrupted public transport, as buses and CNG-powered vehicles remain stranded in long queues at filling stations. The ongoing gas crisis continues to take a heavy toll on daily life, affecting both transport services and household expenses. Drivers and vehicle owners urged the authorities to restore adequate gas supply and ensure sufficient pipeline pressure at CNG filling stations without delay.

item.title: Trump signs new orders restricting birthright citizenship
item.description:
US President Donald Trump dismissed a previous Supreme Court decision on citizenship as “very unfortunate” while signing two new executive orders restricting birthright citizenship on Thursday.
“It was close, but a very, very unfortunate decision,” Trump said of the 6-3 vote top court ruling two months ago.
The ruling rebuked Trump’s previous attempt to challenge the constitutional provision that allows individuals born on US soil automatic citizenship.
Birthright citizenship is enshrined in the 14th ​Amendment of the US Constitution. The rule guarantees citizenship for babies born in the US with only narrow exceptions, such as the children of foreign diplomats or members of an enemy occupying force.
“This was done for a different reason. This ​was done right after the Civil War. This ‌was for the babies of slaves, and what’s happening now?” Trump said on Thursday.
Trump’s close advisor and the architect of his immigration policy, Stephen Miller, said one of the orders signed Thursday seeks to deny birthright citizenship to children of members of “foreign terrorist organizations” as well as “large categories of people who lobby and act on behalf of foreign governments.”
Miller added that the order “ensures that large numbers of people who wrongly (would) be getting birthright citizenship will no longer be eligible for those benefits.”
The second executive order targets what Trump called “birth tourism.” The expression refers to visitors securing visas and traveling to the US so they would give birth while in the country, so their children are entitled to US citizenship.
“That practice of birth tourism is, as of ​the signing of this order, hereby banned. What that means is that no one in the world is anymore allowed to obtain a ​visa for this ‌fraudulent purpose,” Miller added.
Currently, there are no official figures depicting the number of foreigners who come to the US for the explicit purpose of giving birth to obtain citizenship. But the Trump-aligned Center for Immigration Studies claims that between 20,000-25,000 mothers did so 2016-2017.
The White House has argued that the new executive orders do not fall within the limits of the Supreme Court ruling.
Still, the orders are expected to be challenged in court.
“I thought we were going to win it at the Supreme Court,” Trump said on Thursday. ”Unfortunately, we had a bad decision, very unfair decision. Our country suffers because of it and we’re ending it a different way,” Trump said.
Currently, no US law bans so-called birth tourism, but a federal regulation implemented in 2020 during Trump’s first term prohibits using temporary tourist and business visas for the primary purpose of obtaining US citizenship for a newborn.

Ex-JCD leader dies after falling from roof during police chase
item.description:
A former leader of the Jatiyatabadi Chhatra Dal (JCD) allegedly died after falling from the rooftop of a five-storey building while fleeing during a police raid in Savar, on the outskirts of Dhaka, early Friday.
The deceased was identified as Monowarul Hossain Bokshi, 29, a former vice-president of Savar Thana JCD and son of Jafar, a security guard at the Bangladesh Public Administration Training Centre (BPATC). The incident occurred around 12:00am at the BPATC Staff Quarters in Savar.
According to police, Shahariar Kabir Soumi had fled from Pirganj in Rangpur with a young woman following a romantic relationship. The woman's family later filed a missing diary with Pirganj Police Station. Acting on the complaint, a team from Pirganj Police arrived at Savar Model Police Station around 11:00pm on Thursday before conducting a joint raid with Savar police at the residence of Monowarul, the suspect's maternal uncle.
Police said Soumi and the woman had already left the house before officers arrived. Sensing the police presence, Monowarul allegedly ran to the rooftop in an attempt to flee. Police followed him to the roof, where he suddenly fell from the five-storey building.
Officer-in-Charge (OC) Saiful Alam of Savar Model Police Station said the Pirganj police had come to Savar to arrest the suspect and informed the local police, who then joined the operation.
"While the Pirganj police entered the building to apprehend the suspect, a young man fell from the rooftop and died. Members of Savar Model Police Station were stationed outside the building," the OC said.
Police have formed a five-member investigation committee to probe the incident.

The Appellate Division’s chamber court on Thursday stayed the High Court's order granting interim bail to former army member Hafizur Rahman, an accused in the murder case of Comilla’s Sohagi Jahan Tonu, and ordered him to surrender within 24 hours.
If Hafizur fails to surrender within the stipulated time, police have been directed to arrest him, Attorney General Md Ruhul Quddus Kazal said after the hearing.
The order came after the state challenged the High Court's August 2 decision granting Hafizur six months' interim bail.
The High Court bench of Justice Zafar Ahmed and Justice Sathika Hossain had also issued a rule asking why he should not be granted permanent bail and directed the authorities concerned to respond within four weeks.
Following the High Court order, Hafizur was released from jail, prompting the state to move the Appellate Division seeking cancellation of the bail.
Deputy Attorney General Shiuli Khanam and Assistant Attorneys General Sabbir Hossain, Md Mizanur Rahman, Rezaul Karim and Mir Moniruzzaman represented the state, while lawyer Muslem Uddin Bhuiyan appeared for Hafizur.
Hafizur, 52, a former senior warrant officer of the Bangladesh Army, was arrested by the Police Bureau of Investigation (PBI) from his residence in Keraniganj on April 21 in connection with the high-profile murder case.
Tonu, a student and private tutor, went missing on the evening of March 20, 2016, after going to a house inside Comilla Cantonment for a tutoring session. Her body was later recovered from a bush near the cantonment's power house area.
The murder has remained under investigation for years, drawing widespread public attention. Hafizur's arrest earlier this year renewed focus on the long-running case.

item.title: RAB arrests two with rare Sterling submachine gun, foreign pistol in Rajbari raids
item.description:
Members of Rapid Action Battalion (RAB) arrested two alleged armed men and seized a rare foreign-made Sterling submachine gun, a foreign-made pistol and 34 rounds of live ammunition in separate raids in Rajbari's Sadar and Goalanda upazilas.
The arrested men were identified as Md Momin Molla and Hasan Ali Biswas. RAB said they have links to the banned Sarbahara Party's Manju-Jahangir group.
The arrests were made in separate operations conducted by members of RAB-10's CPC-3 Faridpur Camp on Wednesday evening and night, RAB-10 Commanding Officer Additional DIG Md Asaduzzaman told a press conference at the RAB Media Centre in Karwan Bazar on Thursday afternoon.
Company Commander of RAB's Faridpur Camp, Major Farhan Mahmud Moktada, was also present.
Briefing reporters, the Commanding Officer said, acting on a tip-off, its members conducted the first raid at Mahishkhola Mollabari area under Pachuria Union in Rajbari Sadar around 6:45 pm on Wednesday. Momin Molla was arrested during the operation.
RAB recovered a foreign-made Sterling submachine gun, two magazines, 28 rounds of live ammunition and two mobile phones from his possession.
Asaduzzaman said Momin Molla is a Saudi Arabia expatriate who returned to Bangladesh about a month ago and was scheduled to fly back to Saudi Arabia on August 13.
He added that the recovered Sterling submachine gun is an extremely rare type of firearm.
In another operation around 10:15 pm the same day, RAB arrested Hasan Ali Biswas near Jalil Member Bridge in Chhoto Bhakla Union under Goalanda upazila.
During the raid, RAB recovered a foreign-made pistol, one magazine, six rounds of live ammunition, several locally made weapons, four mobile phones and Tk 15,300 in cash from his possession.
The RAB-10 chief said preliminary interrogation revealed that both arrested men have links to the Sarbahara Party, while Hasan Ali Biswas is associated with the party's Manju-Jahangir group.
He said RAB's drive to arrest the group's leader, Manju-Jahangir, is continuing.
He also said local residents had been disturbed by the alleged criminal activities of the arrested men. RAB will seek remand of the accused to identify the source of the weapons, their use and other associates.
RAB said cases under the Arms Act are being filed against the two men with the respective police stations and legal action is underway.

item.title: 'UN withheld July uprising eyewitness identities over death penalty provision'
item.description:
The United Nations did not share the identities of eyewitnesses cited in its fact-finding report on the July 2024 Mass Uprising because Bangladesh's International Crimes Tribunal (ICT) Act still retains the death penalty, a prosecutor told the tribunal on Thursday.
Prosecutor Gazi Monawar Hossain Tamim made the disclosure while presenting arguments before International Crimes Tribunal-2 in a crimes against humanity case against seven leaders of the now-banned Awami League and its affiliated organizations, including Awami League General Secretary Obaidul Quader.
During the hearing, Monawar said armed activists of the Chhatra League and Awami League attacked protesters between July 14 and July 17, 2024, on the instructions of senior party leaders, adding that the incidents were documented in the UN's fact-finding report.
He said the report contains references for all witnesses but the UN had informed the prosecution that it would disclose the identities of eyewitnesses only if the death penalty was removed from Bangladesh's ICT law.
"As a result, we did not receive the UN's eyewitnesses," the prosecutor said, adding that the prosecution is instead producing its own eyewitnesses before the tribunal.
Following the fall of the Awami League government during the Jul uprising, the Office of the United Nations High Commissioner for Human Rights (OHCHR) published a fact-finding report examining events between July 1 and August 15, 2024.
The report held senior leaders of the then-ruling Awami League responsible for atrocities and crimes against humanity committed during the period.
To prepare the report, the UN fact-finding mission conducted investigations in eight cities—Dhaka, Chittagong, Rangpur, Rajshahi, Khulna, Bogra, Sylhet and Gazipur.
It interviewed more than 230 victims and eyewitnesses, along with 36 government officials, members of the security forces and political figures familiar with the events.
Monawar told the tribunal that the UN withheld the identities of those eyewitnesses because the ICT Act still provides for capital punishment. The United Nations has consistently called for the abolition of the death penalty for all crimes.
Besides Obaidul Quader, the accused are Awami League Joint General Secretary AFM Bahauddin Nasim, former state minister for Information and Broadcasting Mohammad Ali Arafat, Jubo League Chairman Sheikh Fazle Shams Parash and General Secretary Mainul Hossain Khan, and Chhatra League President Saddam Hossain and General Secretary Sheikh Wali Asif.
All seven accused are currently absconding.

item.title: Defence adviser: Migration management now part of national security
item.description:
Prime Minister's Defence Adviser Brig Gen (retd) Dr AKM Shamsul Islam on Thursday said migration management has become an integral part of national security amid evolving global and geopolitical realities.
Speaking as the keynote speaker at a program titled Migration Governance as a National Security Instrument in Bangladesh at the Bangladesh University of Professionals (BUP) in Mirpur Cantonment, he said migration is no longer solely an issue of the economy, employment or the labor market.
"It is directly linked to a country's internal stability, border management, humanitarian protection and overall national security," he said.
Shamsul said the concept of national security has expanded beyond protecting territorial boundaries to include safe migration, legal employment opportunities, orderly cross-border movement, and safeguarding the rights and dignity of Bangladeshis living abroad.
He warned that failure to ensure safe, orderly and well-managed migration could create multidimensional challenges for domestic stability, border security and regional peace.
Highlighting the importance of remittances to the economy, he stressed the need to develop a skilled workforce, expand opportunities for safe and regular migration, and equip prospective migrants with adequate knowledge, training and protection.
He also called for stronger coordination among relevant institutions to combat irregular migration, fraud, human trafficking and transnational criminal networks.
Describing Bangladeshi expatriates as valuable contributors to both the national economy and the country's global image, the defence adviser said the state's capacity must be strengthened to protect their rights, security and dignity while providing support during times of crisis.
"A well-coordinated, humane and security-conscious migration system can accelerate Bangladesh's economic progress while reinforcing national security," he said.
He also called for a forward-looking migration policy that integrates the economic, humanitarian, social and security dimensions of migration, emphasizing the importance of policy-oriented research, reliable data, skilled human resources and coordinated institutional efforts.
During an interactive session, BUP students raised questions on migration policy, human trafficking, the safety of Bangladeshi expatriates, border management, regional geopolitics and national security. Responding to the queries, the defence adviser highlighted the growing strategic importance of migration governance in the changing global order.
The event was attended by BUP Vice-Chancellor Maj Gen Md Mahbub-Ul Alam, senior military and civil officials, deans, faculty members, researchers and students.
Concluding the program, the defence adviser praised BUP's contributions to education, research and national development, expressing hope that the university would continue to play an active role in policy research, national dialogue and promoting security awareness among young people.

item.title: Dr Zahid: Family card program to be launched officially on Aug 16
item.description:
Social Welfare Minister Prof Dr A Z M Zahid Hossain on Thursday said the government's Family Card program will be officially launched on August 16 under the 2026–27 fiscal year.
He said Prime Minister Tarique Rahman will inaugurate the program from ward no-8 of Latifabad union in Kishoreganj Sadar Upazila.
The minister said the government plans to bring 4.1 million beneficiaries under the program in its first phase. It is expected that this program will be expanded over the next four years to cover approximately 16 million families across the country.
The decisions were taken at a meeting of the Cabinet Committee on the Family Card program, chaired by Finance Minister Amir Khasru Mahmud Chowdhury at the Bangladesh Secretariat here.
Briefing the reporters after the meeting, Prof Dr Zahid Hossain outlined various aspects of the initiative.
He said the primary objective of the Family Card program is to ensure that government social protection benefits reach genuine beneficiaries while promoting transparency and accountability in the beneficiary selection process.
"No eligible person should be left out, and no ineligible person should be included in the beneficiary list," the minister said, adding that the government is giving the matter the highest priority.
To achieve this, beneficiary information will be updated and reviewed regularly. The database will be revised in line with changes in the socio-economic conditions of households. Families that rise above the poverty line will be removed from the list, while newly eligible households will be added accordingly.
The minister said the government intends to develop the Family Card into a dynamic social registry rather than maintaining it as a static database.
Regular updates based on real-life changes will help to ensure the inclusion of eligible beneficiaries and reduce opportunities for irregularities in social protection programs.
He also said strict verification procedures would be followed at the union level to prevent any errors or irregularities in the distribution process.
Beneficiary information will be verified through local administration, public representatives and relevant officials. Fresh investigations will also be conducted where complaints are received.
According to the minister, the government's goal is to establish an accurate, technology-driven and modern social protection system that reflects changes in people's living conditions through continuous updates to the beneficiary database.
He said the current fiscal year's budget includes a plan to cover 4.1 million beneficiaries under the Family Card program. Following an assessment of its effectiveness, the government aims to expand coverage to around 16 million families over the next four years.
Senior officials from the relevant ministries and divisions attended the Cabinet Committee meeting, where implementation strategies, beneficiary selection, data verification, database management and field-level monitoring of the Family Card programme were discussed in detail.

Others named as accused include former justice AHM Shamsuddin Chowdhury Manik, DU Sociology Department teacher Prof AKM Jamal Uddin and former general secretary of banned Bangladesh Chhatra League Wali Asif Enan.

Govt doctor faces dismissal for private practice during office hours
item.description:
A government doctor is set to face dismissal from service and cancellation of his medical licence after Health Minister Sardar Md Sakhawat Hossain found him allegedly treating patients at a private diagnostic center during official working hours on Thursday.
The doctor, Dr Moinul Hasan Chishti, is posted at Belabo Upazila Health Complex in Narsingdi.
The minister found him during a surprise inspection at Popular Diagnostic Centre on English Road in Old Dhaka and immediately instructed the authorities concerned to revoke his medical licence and dismiss him from government service.
Speaking after the inspection, Sakhawat said government doctors are prohibited from providing medical services at private healthcare facilities during official office hours.
Alleging that Dr Chishti had been violating the rules for a long time, the minister said the doctor's office had previously served him with a show-cause notice, which he allegedly ignored.
"The doctor's office had also served him a show-cause notice, but he ignored it," the minister said.
He also directed the executive magistrate conducting the mobile court to take necessary legal action over the incident.
During the inspection, officials reviewed the clinic's records and found that it did not possess a resignation letter or a no-objection certificate (NOC) indicating that the doctor had resigned from government service or obtained permission to work at a private healthcare facility.
The minister also reprimanded the manager of Popular Diagnostic Centre for allowing a government physician to treat patients without verifying the required documents.
"If a government doctor wants to resign or work elsewhere, a resignation letter and NOC are mandatory. Allowing such practice without verifying these documents is illegal," he said, alleging that the clinic had facilitated unethical practices for financial gain.
The clinic manager acknowledged the lapse, admitting that the authorities had failed to collect the necessary documents from the doctor. He assured the minister that such negligence would not be repeated.
Talking to reporters after the drive, Sakhawat said the government spends substantial public funds to ensure healthcare services at government hospitals.
"If a government doctor neglects official duties to treat patients at a private facility, there will be no leniency," he said.
The minister warned that strict action would be taken against both government doctors and private healthcare institutions found involved in such irregularities.

item.title: City Corporation official dies after falling during warrant execution
item.description:

The deceased was identified as Nazrul Islam, 55, who had an arrest warrant issued against him in a CR (complaint) case pending before a Gazipur court.
The incident took place at around 12:30am at the apartment building located at 63/B Siddheswari Road.
Confirming the incident, Ramna Police Station Sub-Inspector (SI) Md Uzzal said police had gone to the flat to execute the arrest warrant.
"Upon sensing the presence of police, Nazrul may have attempted to flee through the back door and taken shelter on the balcony ledge, or tried to move to a neighbouring flat. He apparently lost his footing during the attempt and fell from the building, sustaining critical injuries," the SI said.
He said Nazrul was rescued and taken to the emergency department of Dhaka Medical College Hospital (DMCH) at around 2:45am, where the on-duty physician declared him dead.
The body has been sent to the DMCH morgue for an autopsy.
Police said the exact circumstances surrounding the incident will be determined following further investigation.

item.title: Govt tightens noise rules, bans night-time honking in residential areas
item.description:
The government has introduced tougher measures to curb noise pollution, including a ban on honking in residential areas between 9:00pm and 6:00am, as part of a new set of restrictions aimed at protecting public health and the environment.
The measures were announced in a public notice issued by the Department of Environment (DoE) on Thursday.
The DoE said noise pollution poses a serious threat to human health and biodiversity. To address the problem, the government has promulgated the Noise Pollution (Control) Rules, 2025, prescribing permissible noise limits for different areas and imposing stricter controls on noise-generating activities.
Under the rules, the maximum allowable noise level has been set at 40 decibels in silent zones and 75 decibels in industrial areas.
The rules also stipulate that:
(A)Noise generated by any equipment or activity must not exceed the prescribed limits.
(B) High-noise equipment may not be used in public places without prior written approval from the competent authority. Even with permission, the noise levelmust not exceed 90 decibels, operation is limited to five hours, and use must end before 11:00pm.
(C) The manufacture, import, storage, sale, display, distribution, marketing, transportation and use of horns exceeding the prescribed noise limits are prohibited.
(D) Honking is strictly prohibited in silent zones, where the use of firecrackers, fireworks and other noise-producing activities is also banned.
(E) Honking is prohibited in residential areas from 9:00pm to 6:00am.
(F)Picnics are banned in natural forests and wildlife habitats, and the use of loudspeakers or other high-noise equipment in such areas is prohibited.
(G)Construction machinery may not be operated between 7:00pm and 7:00am within 500 metres of the boundary of a residential area.
(H)Traffic sergeants or officers of higher rank are empowered to impose on-the-spot penalties for noise pollution offences committed in their presence.
The Department of Environment urged the public to comply with the new rules to help safeguard public health and protect the environment.

With the latest figures, Bangladesh has recorded 17,880 dengue cases and 59 deaths so far this year.
Last year, dengue claimed 413 lives and infected 102,861 people across the country.
In 2024, the mosquito-borne disease caused 575 deaths and infected 101,214 people.

The Election Commission (EC) on Thursday announced the schedule for the presidential election, with voting set to take place on August 20.
EC Senior Secretary Akhtar Ahmed announced the schedule at a press conference at Nirbachan Bhaban in the capital on Thursday.
According to the schedule, nomination papers will be submitted from 10am to 4pm on August 13.
Scrutiny of nomination papers will be held on August 16, while the last date for withdrawal of candidature is August 18.
Voting will take place from 2pm to 5pm on August 20 in the session chamber of the National Parliament.
Chief Election Commissioner AMM Nasir Uddin is the returning officer of the presidential election.
Earlier, the EC received the voter list for the presidential election from the Parliament Secretariat following its request. The voting will not be held in case of a single candidate.
On July 24 last, Mohammed Shahabuddin resigned as president and Speaker Hafiz Uddin Ahmad took charge as the acting president.
The EC, led by Chief Election Commissioner AMM Nasir Uddin, held a meeting with acting Speaker Barrister Kayser Kamal on July 28 in line with the Presidential Election Act, 1991, which obliges the Commission to consult with the Speaker before the announcement of the schedule for the presidential election.
According to Article 123(2) of the Constitution, an election to fill the vacant office of the President must be held within 90 days of the post becoming vacant due to resignation.

IOM Bangladesh launches first photobook on human trafficking survivors
item.description:
The International Organization for Migration (IOM) Bangladesh on Tuesday launched LISTEN, the country's first photobook dedicated exclusively to documenting the diverse realities of human trafficking through visual storytelling and first-hand survivor accounts.
The publication was unveiled at a ceremony at the UN House in Dhaka, attended by senior government officials, UN representatives, diplomats, development partners and civil society members, who reaffirmed their commitment to preventing human trafficking and supporting survivors.
Among those present were IOM Deputy Director General for Operations Ugochi Daniels, Home Affairs Minister Salahuddin Ahmed, Acting UN Resident Coordinator Carol Flore-Smereczniak, and Korea International Cooperation Agency (KOICA) Bangladesh Country Director Jihoon Kim.
Following the launch, the guests inaugurated a photography exhibition featuring selected images and stories from LISTEN, offering an insight into the lived experiences of trafficking survivors through documentary photography and personal narratives.
The publication places survivors' voices at the centre of the conversation, moving beyond statistics to highlight the human impact of trafficking. It brings together the experiences of women, men, girls and boys who have survived different forms of trafficking and exploitation, while exploring the broader social and economic factors that increase vulnerability.
Speaking at the event, Ugochi Daniels said the stories featured in LISTEN represent only a small fraction of those that remain untold.
"Every day, new stories emerge, each revealing the devastating impact of human trafficking. We do not need more stories. Meaningful action begins with listening to survivors and ensuring their experiences inform policies, strengthen prevention efforts and improve protection programs," she said.
Salahuddin Ahmed said Bangladesh had made significant progress in tackling human trafficking but stressed that more work remained.
"Combating this crime requires strong laws, effective enforcement and informed, engaged communities. LISTEN gives survivors a platform to share their experiences and reminds us of our collective responsibility to prevent trafficking and protect those at risk," he said.
Carol Flore-Smereczniak described LISTEN as a significant contribution to raising awareness of human trafficking and emphasized the importance of placing survivors' voices at the centre of efforts to prevent trafficking and protect human rights.
Jihoon Kim reaffirmed KOICA's commitment to supporting survivor-centred responses and strengthening anti-trafficking efforts through its partnership with IOM.
Developed with KOICA's support, LISTEN is part of IOM's broader efforts to prevent trafficking in persons, protect survivors and raise public awareness by promoting a deeper understanding of the different forms of trafficking and the complex circumstances that place people at risk.
The launch also marked the observance of the World Day Against Trafficking in Persons, highlighting the importance of sustained collaboration among the Government of Bangladesh, the United Nations, development partners and civil society to strengthen prevention, protection, prosecution and partnership.
The programme concluded with guests touring the exhibition and engaging with the stories featured in the publication.

item.title: July Mass Uprising Memorial Museum opens to visitors
item.description:
The long-awaited July Mass Uprising Memorial Museum in Dhaka welcomed its first visitors on Thursday, drawing hundreds of people from across the country eager to explore the newly inaugurated site.
However, the opening day was marred by long queues and ticketing confusion, with many visitors reporting sold-out online tickets, an unclear offline ticketing system, and hours of waiting before being allowed inside.
An on-site visit found long queues stretching outside the museum, with many visitors saying they had been waiting since early morning. Several people arrived without tickets, claiming they were unaware that advance booking was required, while others questioned the decision to introduce ticketing. A limited number of visitors were seen entering the museum after noon.
Mohammad Habibur Rahman, who travelled from Noakhali with his father, said they had come to Dhaka solely to visit the museum.
"We came yesterday (Wednesday), but visitors were not allowed in because of the inauguration. So we returned today (Thursday)."
Mohammad Rakib from Gazipur said he had been waiting in line since 9am.
"I knew the museum wouldn't be open to visitors yesterday (Wednesday) because of the inauguration. That's why I came today (Thursday). It's almost noon, but we're still waiting with no explanation."
Faizul Hossain from Jurain, who identified himself as a participant in the July movement, questioned the ticketing system.
"We've been standing here since 8am and got caught in the rain twice. There's no proper offline ticketing, and many of us can't buy tickets online. At the very least, they should tell us why we're not being allowed in."
Raj, who came from Savar with friends, said the online booking system showed all tickets booked until August 10, while no offline ticket counter was visible.
"We arrived around 9am. It's already noon, and we still don't know when we'll be able to enter."
Another visitor from Savar, Mohammad Rana, said he could neither secure an online ticket nor purchase one at the venue despite arriving around 8:30am.
Bablul Akhtar, who came from Farmgate with his son, said they had been waiting since 8am.
"They aren't giving us clear information. Sometimes they let a few people in, then close the gate again. We have no idea when our turn will come."
Abdul Kader, who travelled from Narail, said visitors received conflicting information throughout the morning.
"At first, they said only those with online tickets could enter. Later, they said offline tickets would be available. They keep changing their statements."
Prime Minister Tarique Rahman on Wednesday inaugurated the museum at Sher-e-Bangla Nagar at 9am.
The museum operates a time-slot-based entry system to manage the expected high volume of visitors. Applicants will be informed in advance of their allotted visiting time through the online booking system.

item.title: Dhaka air quality 4th worst in world Thursday morning
item.description:
Dhaka ranked 4th among the world's most polluted cities on Thursday morning, recording an Air Quality Index (AQI) score of 147 at 9:50am.
According to the AQI scale, the city's air quality was classified as “Unhealthy for Sensitive Groups”, poses health risks to children, older adults, and people with heart or lung diseases, while the general public is mostly unaffected.
Portland of USA topped the global pollution list with an AQI score of 168, followed by Kampala of the Uganda with 160 and Kinshasa of DR Congo with 159.
According to AQI standards, a reading between 101 and 150 is considered ‘unhealthy for sensitive groups’, 151 to 200 ‘unhealthy’, 201 to 300 ‘very unhealthy’, while levels above 301 are deemed ‘hazardous’, posing serious health risks.
The AQI, which provides daily updates on air quality, indicates how clean or polluted the air is and highlights potential health impacts.
In Bangladesh, the AQI is calculated based on five major pollutants: particulate matter (PM10 and PM2.5), nitrogen dioxide (NO2), carbon monoxide (CO), sulfur dioxide (SO2), and ozone.
Dhaka has long struggled with air pollution, with air quality typically worsening in winter and improving during the monsoon season.
The World Health Organization estimates that air pollution causes around seven million deaths globally each year, mainly due to stroke, heart disease, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, lung cancer and acute respiratory infections.

item.title: Amit: Political parties must show patience and tolerance to fulfil July aspirations
item.description:
State Minister for Power, Energy and Mineral Resources Anindya Islam Amit on Wednesday said all political parties must exercise patience and tolerance to realise the aspirations of the July movement, stressing that democratic values should be reflected in both words and actions.
Speaking to reporters after a rally and wreath-laying ceremony marking July Mass Uprising Day in Jessore, Amit said the government remains committed to safeguarding human rights, ensuring good governance and protecting freedom of expression.
"To fulfil the aspirations of July, every political party must act with patience and tolerance," he said. "If we use the same rhetoric that the fascists once used, it would show that we have not truly embraced democracy. Political ideologies may differ, but at the end of the day, our shared goal is to build a modern, self-reliant Bangladesh."
Earlier, a colorful procession began at 10:30 am from the premises of the Deputy Commissioner's Office and marched through the town's main roads before concluding at the Martyrs’ Memorial at Bakultala.

DU inaugurates foundation of July Memorial Monument
item.description:
Dhaka University on Wednesday inaugurated the foundation of the July Memorial Monument, which is being built in memory of those killed during the July 2024 mass uprising.
Dhaka University Vice-Chancellor Prof ABM Obaidul Islam inaugurated the project at a ceremony held on the campus.
Among those present were the fathers of martyrs Mir Mughdo, Faiyaz and Yamin, along with the university's Pro-Vice-Chancellors (Academic and Administration), Treasurer, deans of different faculties, the proctor, teachers and university officials.
Speaking at the programme, the vice-chancellor said: "Two years ago today, a new sun rose over Bangladesh through the mass uprising that began on July 1 and culminated on what protesters referred to as '36 July,' or August 5. Sheikh Hasina fled the country with her sister. We have achieved a new Bangladesh through the blood of the martyrs."
He paid tribute to those killed and injured during the uprising and prayed for the eternal peace of the departed souls.
"To preserve the memory of the martyrs of the uprising, we are establishing the July Memorial Monument," he said.
Prof Obaidul alleged that, over the past 17 years, the Awami League government had committed various injustices to consolidate its power while ignoring the will and demands of the people.
"We cannot measure the extent to which people were indiscriminately killed and shot in their own country. There can be no forgiveness for such acts," he said.
The vice-chancellor also said the university had not forgotten what he described as the suppression of dissent under the previous Dhaka University administration.
"We have not forgotten the persecution of dissenting voices," he said, expressing hope that "fascism will never return to this country on the blood of the martyrs."

item.title: Ziaur Rahman killing case: Prosecution seeks Facebook data of Mozaffar
item.description:
The prosecution has written to Meta seeking the Facebook and Messenger data of former army officer Md Mozaffar Hossain, who was arrested over allegations of involvement in the killing of late president Ziaur Rahman.
International Crimes Tribunal (ICT) Prosecutor and IT expert Tanvir Hasan Zoha confirmed the matter to Dhaka Tribune on Wednesday.
According to the prosecution, the request was made after investigators found evidence that Mozaffar had communicated directly with several individuals through Messenger and maintained contact with certain groups. Efforts are also underway to recover his deleted Messenger conversations.
Zoha said the information has been sought to assist the tribunal's ongoing investigation into crimes against humanity.
The prosecution has requested subscriber information, account registration details, all current and previously registered email addresses and phone numbers, complete login history with timestamps, IP addresses and devices used to access the account, browser information, and all Facebook Messenger data, including deleted conversations.
Ziaur Rahman, founder of the BNP and the country's then president, was killed during a military uprising in Chittagong on May 30, 1981.
Investigators allege that former army officer Mozaffar Hossain played a role in the disappearance of Ziaur Rahman's body after the killing. At the time, he held the rank of major in the Bangladesh Army. He went into hiding following the incident, and authorities announced a reward for information leading to his arrest.
After remaining a fugitive for 45 years, he was arrested by Detective Branch (DB) police from Banani in Dhaka on the night of July 15 and was subsequently handed over to the Bangladesh Army.
On July 23, ICT-2 ordered that Mozaffar be shown arrested in a crimes against humanity case linked to the July Mass Uprising. The tribunal also granted investigators two days to interrogate him and directed that he remain in army custody.
Earlier, ICT Chief Prosecutor Md Aminul Islam said investigators had found evidence of regular communication between Mozaffar and retired lieutenant general Masud Uddin Chowdhury.
According to the chief prosecutor, Masud was one of the influential figures in the army-backed caretaker government in 2007 and is currently in custody in a crimes against humanity case. Mozaffar has also been shown arrested in the same case.
Aminul Islam said Mozaffar's trial over the killing of Ziaur Rahman would proceed under military law and is separate from the ICT proceedings.
"Our investigation concerns crimes against humanity. We will examine whether he had any involvement during the Awami League government's 16 years in power. Our judicial process is completely separate," he said.
He added that Mozaffar would remain in army custody and be brought before ICT investigators for questioning whenever necessary. If the allegations are established, he will face trial under the tribunal's applicable laws.

item.title: Land minister: Govt to stand by families of July martyrs, injured
item.description:
Land Minister Mizanur Rahman Minu on Wednesday said the government will continue to stand by the families of the July mass uprising martyrs and the injured, ensuring their treatment, welfare and long-term rehabilitation.
"The government is committed to upholding the sacrifices of the martyrs and the spirit of the student-people's movement against fascism," he told journalists after placing wreaths at the July Memorial Monument at C&B Intersections.
He said plans are underway to ensure long-term financial security for the martyrs' families and reiterated the government's commitment to building a prosperous and discrimination-free Bangladesh in line with the aspirations of the July mass uprising.
Earlier, the minister paid tribute to the martyrs by laying wreaths at the memorial alongside senior officials of the divisional and district administration.
Among those present were Rajshahi Divisional Commissioner A N M Bazlur Rashid, Rajshahi City Corporation Administrator Md Mahfuzur Rahman Riton, Rajshahi Metropolitan Police Commissioner Mohammad Foyzul Kabir, Rajshahi Deputy Commissioner Kazi Shahidul Islam and Rajshahi Zila Parishad Administrator Advocate Ershad Ali Isha.

item.title: 10 injured in clash between Chhatra Dal, Shibir activists at Barisal University
item.description:
At least 10 people were injured in a clash between activists of Chhatra Dal and Chhatra Shibir at Barisal University on Wednesday over allegations that outsiders had joined a campus rally.
The clash broke out in the morning when the university unit of Chhatra Shibir brought out a procession titled "Indomitable July," according to witnesses and campus sources.
An argument reportedly began after Chhatra Dal activists objected to the alleged presence of outsiders in the rally. The altercation later escalated into a clash, followed by several rounds of chase and counter-chase.
Ashiq Ahmed, senior vice-president of the university unit of Chhatra Dal, alleged that Chhatra Shibir had entered the campus with outsiders carrying sticks and flags.
He claimed that Shibir activists attacked Chhatra Dal members after they requested that the programme be held without outsiders, leaving five to six of their activists injured.
Rejecting the allegation, Zakaria Islam Babu, general secretary of the university unit of Chhatra Shibir, said they had been holding a peaceful program marking the anniversary of the July Uprising when Chhatra Dal activists attacked them near the vice-chancellor's gate.
He claimed that around five Shibir activists were injured in the attack and alleged that the incident occurred in the presence of university authorities. Although the university proctor tried to control the situation, the attack continued, he added.
Zakaria also said a complaint had been submitted to the university's vice-chancellor seeking justice over the incident.
Both student organisations blamed each other for triggering the violence.
The university proctor could not be reached for comment.
Belal Hossain, additional deputy commissioner of Barisal Metropolitan Police, said police rushed to the campus after receiving information about the clash.
"Additional police have been deployed on the campus following the incident. We have urged both sides to remain calm," he said.
Earlier on Tuesday, violence erupted as activists of Jatiyatabadi Chhatra Dal (JCD) and Bangladesh Islami Chhatra Shibir clashed at several educational institutions in the capital, leaving dozens injured.

item.title: State July celebration disrupted over documentary controversy
item.description:
A state ceremony marking the second anniversary of the July Mass Uprising descended into protests on Wednesday after audience members accused the government of distorting the movement’s history through an official documentary, forcing ministers to apologise and promise immediate corrections.
The unprecedented disruption unfolded in the presence of Acting President Hafiz Uddin Ahmed Bir Bikram at the Bangladesh-China Friendship Conference Center, where families of July martyrs, injured protesters, students and political activists interrupted the program with chants of “Fake, fake” after the documentary was screened.
The protest briefly threw the nationally televised event into disorder, prompting members of the acting president’s security detail to take positions on the stage and inside the auditorium while several invited foreign guests left the venue amid the commotion.
The controversy centred on allegations that the documentary failed to accurately portray the July uprising, omitted key developments -- particularly the events of August 3 -- and inadequately reflected the sacrifices of protesters and the movement’s leadership.
As slogans echoed through the auditorium, organisers repeatedly appealed for calm, but the protest continued.
Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed eventually addressed the gathering, inviting protesters to speak from the stage and urging them to remain seated.
Seeking to defuse tensions, he requested National Citizen Party (NCP) Member Secretary Akhtar Hossain to address the audience.
Akhtar acknowledged the concerns raised by protesters, saying the documentary contained “inconsistencies” that required correction.
“We have also seen the inconsistencies in the documentary,” he said.
“The events of August 3 are completely absent. We will raise these issues with the government and seek accountability from the ministry. But on this historic day, we must remain calm out of respect for the families of the martyrs.”
Following his appeal, Akhtar and other NCP leaders left the venue after taking permission from the acting president.
As protests continued, Liberation War Affairs Minister Ahmed Aazam Khan returned to the stage and publicly apologised to the audience.
“Today’s documentary has caused you pain,” he said.
“The July movement and the mass uprising belong to all of us. We will carefully review every inconsistency, including the omission of the events of August 3, and take immediate steps to correct them.”
He also assured the audience that the documentary would be reviewed in consultation with representatives of the martyrs’ families and injured July fighters before being revised.
Only after the minister’s apology and commitment to amend the film did the protesters withdraw their objections, allowing the remainder of the program to proceed.
The event, organised by the Ministry of Liberation War Affairs, began with a reception for the families of July martyrs and injured July fighters before the documentary was shown.

item.title: Swapon calls for equitable, accountable state inspired by July Uprising
item.description:
Information and Broadcasting Minister Zahir Uddin Swapon on Wednesday called on all to work together to build an equitable, accountable and humane state inspired by the spirit of the July Mass Uprising.
Speaking at a discussion and reception for families of the July martyrs at the District Shilpakala Academy auditorium in Barishal, organized to mark July Mass Uprising Day 2026, the minister said the ideals of the historic movement must remain alive in the hearts of every citizen.
He said the spirit forged through the sacrifices and aspirations of thousands of people must not be undermined by any force, urging everyone to remain united and vigilant.
Swapon said that a group and a single family had monopolised democracy and people's rights for years, weakening democratic institutions and depriving citizens of their voting rights.
He urged people from all walks of life, regardless of political affiliation, religion or ethnicity, to forge unity to protect democracy.
The minister said attempts had been made to divide people through intimidation, greed and promises of power, but conscious citizens rejected such temptations and prioritised the country's interests.
He emphasized that the July Mass Uprising was not the work of a few individuals but a collective resistance against prolonged deprivation, injustice and oppression.
The strength of this movement is laying in the unity, courage and unwavering faith of the people in democracy, he said.
Barisal Divisional Commissioner Khalil Ahmed chaired the program, where government officials, political leaders, media representatives and families of the July martyrs were present.
A documentary on the July martyrs was also screened.

item.title: Sand-laden trucks outside Khaleda Zia's residence: Ex-joint secretary sent to jail
item.description:
A Dhaka court on Wednesday sent former joint secretary Syed Jaglul Pasha to jail in a case over allegations that he helped obstruct former prime minister Khaleda Zia from attending a political rally in 2013 by barricading the road outside her Gulshan residence with sand-laden trucks and using pepper spray.
Dhaka Metropolitan Magistrate Kamal Uddin passed the order after Gulshan Zonal Team Inspector Anwar Hossain produced Jaglul Pasha before the court and sought a 10-day remand. The court fixed Thursday for the remand hearing. SI Mokhtar Hossain of the prosecution confirmed the matter
Jaglul was arrested by the Dhaka Metropolitan Police's Detective Branch (DB) from his Bashundhara residence at around 1:30am on Tuesday.
According to the case statement, Jaglul was among 111 named accused, along with 250-300 unidentified individuals, who allegedly gathered outside Khaleda Zia's Gulshan residence on December 28, 2013, armed with deadly weapons. They allegedly remained there throughout the day, assaulted BNP leaders and activists, carried out acts of sabotage by blocking roads, and created obstacles to prevent Khaleda Zia from attending a scheduled political rally.
The complaint further alleged that at around 9am on December 29, 2013, when Khaleda Zia was preparing to leave for the rally with her entourage, the accused barricaded the road with sand-laden trucks and other vehicles. Despite repeated attempts to leave, they allegedly prevented her movement and used banned pepper spray with the intent to kill, leaving Khaleda Zia and several leaders and activists accompanying her injured.
The case was filed at Gulshan Police Station in October 2024 by Shariful Islam Shawon, former joint secretary of the Latif Hall unit of Rajshahi University Chhatra Dal.
Jaglul Pasha also faces allegations in the Zia Orphanage Trust case of preparing forged documents and giving false testimony before the court in proceedings involving former prime minister Khaleda Zia.

item.title: Three everyday kitchen items that could be harming your health
item.description:
Some everyday kitchen items—including old sponges, damaged non-stick pans, and dishwashing liquids with harsh chemicals—can pose hidden health risks if they are not used or replaced properly. Experts say simple changes in your kitchen routine can help reduce the risk of foodborne illness and unnecessary chemical exposure.
Old kitchen sponge
Kitchen sponges stay damp for long periods, making them an ideal breeding ground for bacteria and fungi. Over time, they can harbor harmful bacteria such as Salmonella and E. coli . These microbes can contaminate dishes and food, increasing the risk of foodborne illness, including diarrhea, vomiting, stomach infections, and fever.
When to replace it:
Dishwashing liquid with harsh chemicals
Some dishwashing liquids contain artificial fragrances, dyes, and other chemicals that may cause irritation in sensitive individuals. If dishes are not rinsed thoroughly, small amounts of residue may remain on the surface. In some people, this may contribute to skin irritation, dermatitis, eye irritation, or respiratory discomfort.
How to use it safely:
Damaged non-stick pan
A non-stick pan with deep scratches or a peeling coating should be replaced. Tiny particles from the damaged coating may end up in food, while overheating worn non-stick cookware can release fumes that may irritate the eyes and throat and cause temporary flu-like symptoms known as polymer fume fever.
Experts also recommend avoiding overheating non-stick cookware and considering alternatives such as stainless steel, cast iron, or tri-ply cookware.
Safe cookware practices:
Small changes can make a big difference
These kitchen items are not inherently dangerous, but improper use or failure to replace them regularly can increase health risks. Simple habits—such as replacing your sponge regularly, choosing gentler cleaning products, and discarding damaged cookware—can help reduce the risk of foodborne illness and unnecessary exposure to potentially harmful substances.

item.title: Measles outbreak: Death toll reaches 854 as five die in 24 hours
item.description:
Five more children have died from measles-like symptoms in the 24 hours leading up to 8:00am on Wednesday, raising the overall death toll from the ongoing outbreak to 854.
The Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS) has classified all five of the latest casualties as suspected.
With the latest figures, the total number of suspected measles deaths has reached 758, while the number of confirmed deaths remained unchanged at 96, as no new confirmed measles deaths were reported in the last 24 hours.
Among the five new suspected fatalities, the highest concentration was recorded in Dhaka, with three deaths reported in both the Dhaka division and Dhaka district.
A total of 959 suspected measles cases were recorded in the 24 hours till Wednesday morning, taking the overall suspected case tally to 132,905.
During the same period, 124 new confirmed measles cases were reported, bringing the total number of confirmed infections to 16,655.
Since March 15, 2026, a total of 115,234 suspected measles patients have been hospitalized across the country, of whom 111,005 have recovered and been discharged from hospitals, according to the DGHS.

Azam Khan: Govt to implement July Charter in spirit of July Uprising
item.description:
Liberation War Affairs Minister Ahmed Azam Khan on wednesday said the government would implement the July Charter in the spirit of the July Uprising, expressing optimism that the movement had paved the way for a prosperous and democratic Bangladesh.
"We will implement the July Charter in the spirit of the July Uprising. People now want prosperity and democracy. We believe that the uprising has brought about a significant transformation," he said.
The minister made the remarks after laying a wreath at the July Martyr Memorial in Shahbagh this morning on the occasion of July Mass Uprising Day.
Azam Khan said the uprising was not merely a mass movement but the beginning of a new chapter of political and institutional reforms.
He said the elected government, led by Prime Minister Tarique Rahman had begun the journey of rebuilding the country by drawing inspiration from the spirit of the uprising.
"Prime Minister Tarique Rahman has started the journey of rebuilding the country alongside the entire nation. He also tirelessly guided the July Mass Uprising," the minister said.
Referring to the political background of the uprising, Azam Khan said it was the outcome of an 18-year struggle by political parties, including the BNP, together with students and people from all walks of life.
He called on all political parties and leaders to preserve national unity.
"I request everyone not to divide the nation over narrow personal interests. The people have united for a prosperous and democratic country. If anyone tries to behave like the fallen fascist regime and divide the nation again, the public will not accept it," he said.
The minister also said freedom of speech had been restored and that the government, under the leadership of Prime Minister Tarique Rahman, would continue working to build a prosperous Bangladesh.
